Functional assays further demonstrated that TBI-derived exosomes enhanced microglial cell migration in vitro.
key_finding_ja: 外傷性脳損傷後に脳組織から分泌されるエキソソームが走化性関連タンパク質を含み、ミクログリアの遊走を促進することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳損傷後のエキソソームを介した神経炎症制御機構の理解が進むことで、脳創傷における炎症抑制の新たな治療標的同定につながる可能性があります。

title: Associations of smoking, aging, and their interplay with the gut microbiome and chronic disease risk profiles.
abstract: Introduction Smoking and aging are both linked to chronic disease and gut microbiome, but their joint relationship with microbiome composition remains uncharacterized. This study examined the overlap between smoking- and age-associated gut microbial signals and their associations with cardiovascular diseases. Methods We analyzed 6676 participants from a filtered project-specific metadata subset from the Guangdong Gut Microbiome Project together with the public GGMP OTU table. Associations of smoking phenotypes and aging with gut microbiota were examined using multivariable linear models. Additional sensitivity analyses were performed in males only, and robustness analyses were repeated at the family and genus levels. Results We identified 222 OTUs associated with first-hand smoking and 117 OTUs associated with second-hand smoke exposure. Among never smokers, age was associated with 330 OTUs. Eighty-five OTUs overlapped between smoking- and age-associated signals. Differences in the abundance of these OTU groups between never smokers and daily smokers were more pronounced in younger than older age strata. The smoking- and age-related OTU groups were associated with several cardiometabolic markers, and mediation analysis suggested that systolic blood pressure may partly account for the association between this overlapping microbial signal and ASCVD risk score. In a male-only sensitivity analysis, the central smoking-aging microbial signal remained directionally consistent. Family- and genus-level robustness analyses also supported persistence of selected associations. Conclusions In this cross-sectional secondary analysis, smoking and aging were associated with overlapping gut microbiome patterns, with stronger smoking-related deviations in younger adults. These findings support future longitudinal studies of microbiome-linked cardiovascular risk in smoking-exposed populations.
authors: Bao Z, Yang Z, Sun R, Meng R, Wu W, Li MD.
journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
screening_reason: The study centers on mapping gut microbiome composition shifts associated with smoking and aging and their relationship to cardiovascular risk.
summary_ja: Guangdong Gut Microbiome Projectのデータ（6,676名）を用いて、喫煙と加齢が腸内細菌叢に与える重複した影響を解析しました。喫煙関連および加齢関連のOTUのうち85個が重複しており、日常喫煙による菌叢の偏りは高齢層よりも若年層でより著しいことが判明しました。また、この重複する微生物シグナルは心血管代謝マーカーやASCVDリスクスコアと関連しており、収縮期血圧がその媒介因子の一部である可能性が示唆されました。
summary_en: Analyzing 6,676 participants from a large microbiome project, researchers evaluated overlapping gut microbial signatures associated with smoking and aging. They identified 85 operational taxonomic units shared between smoking- and age-associated signals, with more pronounced smoking-related differences observed in younger age strata. Mediation analysis suggested that blood pressure may partially account for the relationship between this microbial signal and cardiovascular risk.
key_finding_ja: 喫煙と加齢は重複する腸内細菌叢パターンと関連しており、若年者において喫煙に伴う菌叢変化がより顕著であった。
why_it_matters_ja: 喫煙と加齢に共通する菌叢シグナルが心血管リスクに関連することを示す結果であり、環境要因と加齢が微細生態系に与える影響の解明に繋がります。

title: ADP-ribosylation: An emerging regulator of the epigenome.
abstract: ADP-ribosylation (ADPRylation) is a post-translational modification best known for its roles in DNA damage responses and cytoplasmic signaling, but it also serves important functions in epigenome regulation. In the nucleus, ADPRylation modulates chromatin structure and gene expression through the coordinated modification of histones and chromatin-associated proteins. Although poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation (PARylation) has dominated the field, particularly as therapeutic targets in DNA repair deficient malignancies, a gap remains in our understanding of how mono(ADP-ribosyl)ation (MARylation)-mediated by mono(ADP-ribosyl) transferases (MARTs)-functions as a discrete, site-specific epigenomic mark. Nuclear MART-mediated ADPRylation modulates the activity, localization, and complex assembly of epigenomic enzymes, and directly modifies histones to influence chromatin accessibility and transcriptional dynamics. These reversible modifications intersect with canonical epigenomic marks, enabling rapid, context-dependent control of gene expression. Emerging studies further implicate dysregulated nuclear ADPRylation in cancer, where altered MARylation of chromatin regulators and transcription factors contributes to aberrant gene expression programs and may represent a novel class of therapeutic vulnerabilities. In this review, we synthesize emerging insights into nuclear ADPRylation, with a focus on MART-mediated regulation of histones and chromatin enzymes, and discuss how this regulatory layer expands current models of epigenomic control in physiology and how its alterations drive oncogenesis, offering novel, nonsynthetically lethal avenues for targeted cancer therapy.
authors: Camacho CV, Liu C, Kraus WL.
screening_reason: Focuses entirely on the mechanisms and biological roles of ADP-ribosylation as a protein post-translational modification.
summary_ja: 本総説では、翻訳後修飾の一種であるADPリボシル化（ADPRylation）がエピゲノムやクロマチン構造を調節する役割について解説しています。特にモノADPリボシル化転移酵素（MART）を介したモノADPリボシル化（MARylation）が、ヒストンやクロマチン関連酵素の機能や局在を動的に変化させるメカニズムに焦点を当てています。さらに、がんにおける核内ADPリボシル化の異常と、それを標的とした新たな治療法への応用可能性を議論しています。
summary_en: This review highlights the emerging role of nuclear ADP-ribosylation as a key post-translational modification regulating the epigenome and chromatin structure. It focuses on mono(ADP-ribosyl)ation mediated by MARTs and its capacity to modulate histones and chromatin enzymes. The authors also discuss how dysregulated ADP-ribosylation contributes to oncogenesis and provides potential novel therapeutic targets.
key_finding_ja: モノADPリボシル化を中心とする核内ADPリボシル化が、クロマチン構造と遺伝子発現を精密に調節する重要な翻訳後修飾層であることが提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: ADPリボシル化によるエピゲノム制御機構の解明は、がん治療における新たな分子標的の同定につながる可能性があります。

title: PIWI-piRNA Axis in Epilepsy: Bridging Epigenetic Regulation, Neuroinflammation, and Neuronal Excitability.
abstract: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, neuroinflammation, and epigenetic instability, with around one-third of patients experiencing drug-resistant epilepsy. While ion channels and neurotransmitter imbalances have been thoroughly examined in relation to epilepsy, the significance of piRNAs and their interaction with PIWI proteins in gene regulation, transposon silencing, and inflammatory signaling inside the epileptic brain is gaining recognition. This summary encapsulates the existing understanding of piRNA synthesis, the epigenetic control through PIWI-piRNA interactions, and their novel roles in epileptogenesis. PIWI-piRNA complexes target highly expressed genomic areas, such as LINE-1 retrotransposons, and mute them by recruiting chromatin modifiers such DNMT3A and H3K9 methyltransferase complexes, therefore influencing genome stability and neuronal excitability. Additionally, piRNAs initiate pathways associated with neuroinflammation, including the activation of the Toll-like receptor-4/NF-kB signaling pathway and the NLRP3 inflammasome, and indirectly influence GABAergic homeostasis through interactions with the extensive noncoding RNA regulatory network. Targeted modulation of kainic acid, pilocarpine, and hereditary epilepsy models has been documented to provide decreases in seizure load; however, the extent of this effect varies among the models and modulation techniques employed. The review critically evaluates emerging therapeutic strategies, including AAV9 vectors, lipid nanoparticles, exosome-based delivery systems, and antisense oligonucleotides, along with their associated challenges such as blood-brain barrier penetration, off-target effects, immune activation, and long-term safety. In conclusion, the PIWI-piRNA axis represents a potential yet nascent domain for biomarker creation and disease modulation in epilepsy.
authors: Shyam M, Rashmi R, Sharma V, Venkatesh R, Jain A, G Y, Gopalakrishnan AV, Srirangan P, Prince SE.
screening_reason: Examines the PIWI-piRNA axis in modulating neuroinflammatory pathways (TLR4/NF-kB and NLRP3) in the context of epilepsy.
summary_ja: てんかんの病態生理におけるPIWI-piRNA軸のエピジェネティクス修飾、神経炎症、および神経興奮性に対する役割を整理したレビューである。PIWI-piRNA複合体によるエピジェネティック制御がレトロトランスポゾンをサイレンシングし、ゲノム安定性と神経興奮性に影響を与えるメカニズムが論じられている。さらに、piRNAがTLR4/NF-κB経路やNLRP3インフラマソームを介して神経炎症を誘導・修飾する機構や、GABA作動性ホームオスタシスへの関与を解説している。AAV9や脂質ナノ粒子、核酸医薬を用いた治療応用への課題と展望についても議論されている。
summary_en: This review highlights the role of the PIWI-piRNA axis in epilepsy, bridging epigenetic gene regulation, neuroinflammation, and neuronal excitability. PIWI-piRNA complexes target retrotransposons to influence genome stability while modulating inflammatory signaling pathways such as TLR4/NF-κB and the NLRP3 inflammasome. Targeted modulation of this axis shows potential in reducing seizure burden in experimental models, positioning it as an emerging target for therapy.
key_finding_ja: てんかん病態においてPIWI-piRNA軸はゲノム安定性の維持だけでなく、TLR4/NF-κBやNLRP3を介した神経炎症反応および神経興奮性を調節している。
why_it_matters_ja: PIWI-piRNA軸を標的とした介入は薬剤耐性てんかんの新たなバイオマーカーや治療戦略となる可能性があるが、送達技術や安全性に関する更なる検証が必要である。

title: Continuous theta burst stimulation delays L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia progression and ameliorates orolingual dyskinesia with concomitant reduction of striatal FosB/ΔFosB and neuroinflammation.
abstract: Chronic L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA) administration in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) inevitably leads to L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID), which can be more disabling than PD itself. Therefore, finding ways to prevent or delay LID progression is crucial. Continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS), a patterned form of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, shows promise to alleviate LID. However, whether it can prevent or delay LID progression and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. In this study, we administered L-DOPA daily with or without concurrent cTBS to hemiparkinsonian rats for 3 weeks. Electromagnetic simulation confirmed that the dorsolateral striatum is within the electromagnetic field generated by cTBS. Prolonged L-DOPA administration deteriorated LID progressively, whereas cTBS significantly delayed the development of axial, limb, and total dyskinesia, with orolingual dyskinesia even improving over time. Additionally, L-DOPA administration significantly increased the number of FosB/ΔFosB⁺ cells and CD68⁺/Iba1⁺ cells, with elevated iNOS, IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels, without altering total microglial numbers in the dorsolateral striatum. cTBS reversed all these changes, reducing FosB/ΔFosB⁺ cells, CD68⁺/Iba1⁺ cells, and all 4 pro-inflammatory markers. Furthermore, FosB/ΔFosB⁺ cell numbers and pro-inflammatory marker levels positively correlated with the severity of total, axial, limb, and orolingual dyskinesia. Collectively, cTBS treatment delays the progression of LID and improves orolingual dyskinesia, which is closely associated with the reduction of FosB/∆FosB + cells and alleviation of microglia-related inflammation in the striatum.
authors: Wu X, Sun Q, Yang S, Wang Y, Bai Y, Hui Y, Li L, Qiao H, Zhang Q, Wang L.
screening_reason: The study directly measures and evaluates the reduction of striatal microglial activation and neuroinflammation following continuous theta burst stimulation.
summary_ja: ヘミパーキンソン病ラットモデルにおいて、L-DOPAの長期投与に持続的シータバースト刺激（cTBS）を併用する効果が検証された。L-DOPA単独投与はジスキネジアを進行させたが、cTBSの併用は軸性、四肢性、および総ジスキネジアの進行を遅らせ、口舌部ジスキネジアを改善した。また、cTBSは背外側線条体におけるFosB/ΔFosB陽性細胞数およびミクログリアに関連する炎症性マーカーの上昇を抑制した。これらの変化の抑制はジスキネジアの軽減と相関していた。
summary_en: In hemiparkinsonian rats, continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) combined with L-DOPA administration delayed the progression of axial, limb, and total dyskinesia while improving orolingual dyskinesia. Concurrently, cTBS reduced the accumulation of striatal FosB/ΔFosB-positive cells and suppressed microglial neuroinflammatory markers. These findings indicate that cTBS delays L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia progression in association with reduced striatal FosB/ΔFosB expression and neuroinflammation.
key_finding_ja: ヘミパーキンソン病ラットにおいて、cTBSの併用はL-DOPA誘発性ジスキネジアの進行を遅らせるとともに、線条体におけるFosB/ΔFosBの発現とミクログリア主導の神経炎症を抑制した。
why_it_matters_ja: L-DOPA誘発性ジスキネジアに対する神経刺激療法のメカニズムとして神経炎症の抑制が示唆され、新たな治療アプローチの開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: The gut-brain-mitophagy axis: Urolithin A as a transcriptional activator of Parkin in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a cardinal, causative, and convergent hallmark in both Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). However, therapeutics that target the process of mitophagy, the selective removal of damaged mitochondria, are relatively undeveloped. Prior work has largely centered around post-translational modifications of the PINK1-Parkin signaling pathway while ignoring the key need for sustained protein synthesis of Parkin. In this review, we explore an innovative transcriptional circuit involving the gut microbiome, AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), and mitophagy: gut-derived metabolites, such as Urolithin A (UA), activate AMPK and SIRT1, both of which converge to deacetylate and phosphorylate peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α). The transcription of the mitophagy protein, Parkin, is then driven by activation of PGC-1α. This UA/AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α/Parkin/mitophagy pathway is disrupted in multiple layers in AD and PD; this includes impaired gut function, lowering the level of UA produced in the body, proteinopathy leading to reduced PGC-1α activity, and decreased transcription of Parkin. Therapeutic targets of these various nodes include UA, PGC-1α activator ZLN005, and SIRT1 activators, such as resveratrol or nicotinamide riboside. By shifting the paradigm from post-translational activation to transcriptional restoration of Parkin, this gut-brain metabolic axis offers a unifying, testable, and therapeutically tractable framework for mitigating mitophagy failure in AD and PD.
authors: Shokr MM, Fawzy MN.
screening_reason: Focuses on the gut-brain metabolic axis involving gut-derived Urolithin A in regulation of mitophagy in neurodegenerative diseases.
summary_ja: アルツハイマー病やパーキンソン病におけるミトコンドリア機能障害に対し、腸脳代謝軸を介したマイトファジー促進経路が論じられています。腸内細菌由来代謝物であるウロリチンA（UA）は、AMPKおよびSIRT1を活性化し、PGC-1αを介してParkinの転写を誘導することが整理されています。神経変性疾患ではこの腸内細菌代謝物産生や転写回路の障害が観察されるため、転写レベルでのParkin回復が重要な戦略となります。UAやPGC-1α/SIRT1活性化剤を用いた本経路への介入が、新たな治療法として提示されています。
summary_en: This review highlights a gut-brain metabolic axis where the gut-derived metabolite Urolithin A (UA) activates AMPK and SIRT1, driving PGC-1a-mediated transcription of Parkin to promote mitophagy. Disruption of this UA/AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1a/Parkin pathway is implicated in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Reinstating Parkin synthesis via transcriptional targeted therapeutics, such as UA and SIRT1 activators, represents a promising paradigm for treating neurodegenerative diseases.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌由来のウロリチンAがAMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α経路を介してParkinの転写を活性化し、神経変性疾患におけるマイトファジー不全を改善する機序が提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 翻訳後修飾だけでなくParkinの転写促進に着目した腸脳軸アプローチは、アルツハイマー病やパーキンソン病におけるミトコンドリア除去不全の治療法開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Targeting Microglial C5aR1 with PMX205 Attenuates Neuroinflammation and Improves Neurological Recovery After Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Activation of microglia and inflammatory response play a central role in the pathological process following intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). In this study, single-nucleus transcriptomic and proteomic profiling was performed to investigate microglial changes after ICH. A significant upregulation of complement receptor C5aR1 was identified, particularly enriched in microglial subsets exhibiting a pro-inflammatory phenotype. The cellular localization and temporal expression dynamics of C5aR1 were validated by immunofluorescence staining, Western blotting, and quantitative PCR, demonstrating its sustained elevation in microglia after ICH. Pharmacological inhibition with the selective C5aR1 antagonist PMX205 markedly reduced the release of inflammatory cytokines, alleviated neuronal damage, and improved neurological function. Proteomic profiling and subsequent validation suggested that CCR5 may be associated with C5aR1-related inflammatory responses after ICH. Collectively, these findings suggest that C5aR1 serves as a regulatory factor in microglia-mediated neuroinflammation following ICH, and that targeting this pathway may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for hemorrhagic stroke.
authors: Shi X, Li X, Ding H, Cao C, Liu J, Li S, Qiu Y, Li H, Li X.
screening_reason: Investigates microglial C5aR1 regulation of neuroinflammation and neurological recovery following intracerebral hemorrhage.
summary_ja: 脳出血（ICH）後の小膠細胞（ミクログリア）の活性化と炎症反応の網羅的解析が行われました。単一核トランスクリプトームおよびプロテオーム解析により、炎症性フェノタイプを示すミクログリアサブセットで補体受容体C5aR1の発現が著しく上昇していることが見出されました。選択的C5aR1拮抗薬であるPMX205の投与は、炎症性サイトカインの放出を抑制し、神経損傷を軽減して神経機能の回復を改善しました。さらにプロテオーム解析から、CCR5がC5aR1に関連する炎症反応に関与している可能性が示唆されました。
summary_en: Single-nucleus transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed a significant upregulation of complement receptor C5aR1 in pro-inflammatory microglial subsets after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Pharmacological inhibition of C5aR1 using PMX205 attenuated inflammatory cytokine release, reduced neuronal damage, and enhanced neurological recovery in animal models. Proteomic profiling further implicated CCR5 in C5aR1-associated neuroinflammatory pathways following ICH.
key_finding_ja: 脳出血後のミクログリアにおいてC5aR1が持続的に発現上昇しており、その薬理学的阻害により神経炎症が抑制され神経機能の回復が促進されることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳出血後のミクログリア主導の神経炎症を制御する新たな標的としてC5aR1が有望であり、出血性脳卒中の治療法開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Rutin ameliorates perioperative neurocognitive disorders by inhibiting microglial HIF-1α/PKM2‑driven glycolysis.
abstract: Background Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) are common complications in elderly patients, largely driven by microglia-mediated neuroinflammation. Rutin, a natural flavonoid, exhibits anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects, but its role in PND remains unclear. Methods An abdominal surgery-induced PND model was established in aged mice. Behavioral performance was assessed using the Morris Water Maze and Fear Conditioning Test. Hippocampal tissues were collected to evaluate microglial activation, synaptic integrity, and neuroinflammatory markers. Glycolytic metabolism was assessed by measuring lactate levels and expression of glycolysis-related genes and proteins (HIF-1α, PKM2). In vitro studies using LPS-stimulated BV2 microglial cells were performed to validate the metabolic regulatory effects of rutin, including Seahorse analysis of glycolytic flux and HIF-1α overexpression. Results Surgery-induced cognitive impairment was associated with robust microglial activation, synaptic loss, and increased hippocampal expression of HIF-1α and PKM2. Rutin treatment significantly improved cognitive performance, attenuated microglial pro-inflammatory polarization, restored synaptic protein expression, and reduced neuroinflammation. Mechanistically, rutin suppressed glycolytic activity in vivo and in vitro, as evidenced by decreased lactate production, reduced glycolytic gene expression, and normalized extracellular acidification rates. The anti-glycolytic and anti-inflammatory effects of rutin in microglia were partially reversed by HIF-1α overexpression. Conclusion Rutin alleviates surgery-induced cognitive impairment by inhibiting microglial glycolytic reprogramming via the HIF-1α/PKM2 pathway. These findings identify microglial immunometabolism as a therapeutic target in PND and position rutin as a promising candidate for neuroprotection in the perioperative setting.
authors: Li M, Hong R, Tian X, Zong C.
screening_reason: Focuses on microglia-mediated neuroinflammation and microglial immunometabolism in perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
summary_ja: 本研究では、周術期神経認知障害（PND）に対する天然フラボノイドであるルチンの予防・治療効果とそのメカニズムを高齢マウスモデル等で検証しました。開腹手術により誘導された認知機能障害において、ミクログリアの活性化と海馬のHIF-1α/PKM2依存的糖解系代謝の上昇が確認されました。ルチン投与はミクログリアのプロ炎症性分極を抑え、シグナル経路を阻害することで解糖系亢進と神経炎症を抑制し、認知機能を改善しました。さらに、HIF-1αの過剰発現によりルチンの抗解糖・抗炎症作用が一部解除されることがインビトロ実験で確認されました。
summary_en: This study investigated the neuroprotective effect of rutin in an aged mouse model of surgery-induced perioperative neurocognitive disorder. Surgery promoted microglial activation and upregulated HIF-1a/PKM2-driven glycolysis in the hippocampus. Rutin treatment attenuated microglial pro-inflammatory polarization and cognitive deficits by suppressing microglial glycolytic reprogramming via the HIF-1a/PKM2 pathway.
key_finding_ja: ルチンはミクログリアのHIF-1α/PKM2経路依存的な糖解系代謝を抑制することで手術誘発性認知機能障害を改善する。
why_it_matters_ja: 周術期神経認知障害に対するミクログリア免疫代謝を標的とした新たな治療アプローチとして期待されます。

title: Microglial immunometabolism in Alzheimer's disease: A stage-resolved trajectory from adaptive remodeling to the metabolic paradox.
abstract: Microglia are central regulators of the cellular phase of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Under chronic exposure to amyloid-β, pathological tau, and aging-associated bioenergetic decline, these cells undergo immunometabolic remodeling that may initially be adaptive. As stress persists, this remodeling can become maladaptive, marked by disordered glycolysis, disturbed lipid handling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and compensatory failure. In this review, we organize these changes as a stage-dependent trajectory from adaptive remodeling to functional decompensation. We introduce the "metabolic paradox" as an operational descriptor: a concurrent, same-cell mismatch between increased substrate uptake or inflammatory activation and declining bioenergetic efficiency and homeostatic function. Along this trajectory we examine neurovascular energy bottlenecks, substrate redistribution, triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2)/apolipoprotein E (APOE)-dependent lipid homeostasis, mitochondrial and proteostatic collapse, and their links to persistent neuroinflammation, defective phagocytosis, aberrant synaptic pruning, and senescence-like dysfunction. We synthesize prior primary findings and stratify each major claim by evidentiary strength, avoiding the overinterpretation of model-specific results as patient-level mechanisms. Finally, we frame immunoprevention as mechanism-based, early-stage metabolic intervention to preserve homeostatic microglial function, a strategy whose clinical benefit remains a hypothesis requiring prospective testing.
authors: Zou Y, Ou Y, Zhao H, Chen G, Chen Z, Li Y, Jiang J.
screening_reason: The review focuses on microglial immunometabolism and its causal connection to persistent neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: アルツハイマー病（AD）におけるミクログリアの免疫代謝リモデリングについて、適応的変化から機能不全に至る病期依存的な軌跡を考察したレビューである。アミロイドβやタウ蛋白質の蓄積および加齢によるエネルギー代謝低下に対し、ミクログリアは初期には適応的に応答するが、持続的ストレスにより代謝不全が生じる。著者らは、基質取り込みや炎症活性化が増加しながらもエネルギー効率や恒常性維持が低下する現象を「代謝パラドックス」として概念化している。初期段階での代謝的介入による免疫予防可能性を提唱しているが、その臨床的有効性は今後の検証課題である。
summary_en: This review outlines a stage-dependent trajectory of microglial immunometabolic changes in Alzheimer's disease, progressing from adaptive remodeling to functional decompensation. It conceptualizes the "metabolic paradox," wherein microglia exhibit increased substrate uptake alongside impaired bioenergetic efficiency and homeostatic function. Early-stage metabolic interventions are proposed as a potential immunopreventive strategy to preserve homeostatic microglial function.
key_finding_ja: アルツハイマー病におけるミクログリアの免疫代謝変化は、初期の適応的応答から基質取り込みとエネルギー効率低下が同居する「代謝パラドックス」を経て機能障害へと進行する。
why_it_matters_ja: ミクログリアの代謝不全メカニズムの解明は、アルツハイマー病の発症初期における新たな免疫予防的治療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Immunological drivers of oxidative stress in glaucoma: implications for antioxidant therapy.
abstract: Glaucoma is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by RGC loss and irreversible visual impairment, representing the second leading cause of global blindness. Immune-inflammatory responses and oxidative stress are core pathological drivers of glaucomatous optic nerve degeneration, forming a vicious cycle via the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome axis, complement overactivation, and dysregulation of the endogenous antioxidant system. These processes trigger sustained neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and RGC apoptosis. Antioxidant therapies targeting the immune-oxidative stress axis have emerged as promising neuroprotective strategies, including classic antioxidants, Nrf2 activators (e.g., NOB), nanocarrier-mediated targeted delivery systems, and PBM. This mini-review summarizes key molecular mechanisms linking immune activation and oxidative damage in glaucoma, reviews recent advances in the development of antioxidant therapeutics, and discusses current challenges and future directions for clinical translation.
authors: Lin B, Fan W, Li DK.
journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
screening_reason: Reviews the neuroimmunological pathways, immune-inflammatory responses, and neuroinflammation driving optic nerve degeneration in glaucoma.
summary_ja: 緑内障は網膜神経節細胞の脱落と不可逆的な視力障害を特徴とする進行性神経変性疾患です。本ミニレビューでは、TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3インフラマソーム軸や補体過剰活性化を介した免疫炎症応答と酸化ストレスの悪循環機構が整理されています。さらに、Nrf2活性化剤やナノ粒子ドラッグデリバリーなどの抗酸化標的療法の進行状況と臨床応用に向けた課題が論じられています。
summary_en: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by retinal ganglion cell loss and visual impairment driven by neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms linking immune-inflammatory activation and oxidative damage, such as the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis. It also discusses novel therapeutic strategies targeting the immune-oxidative stress axis and key challenges for clinical translation.
key_finding_ja: 緑内障における神経変性は免疫応答と酸化ストレスの悪循環により増幅され、これを標的とした抗酸化療法が新しい神経保護戦略として期待される。
why_it_matters_ja: 本解説は前臨床試験や概念実証段階の知見を中心にまとめられており、実際の臨床治療に導入するにはさらなるヒトでの検証が必要です。

title: Discovery of Anti-Neuroinflammatory Compounds in Alzheimer's Disease: Current Trends and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation in response to abnormal protein aggregates has been implicated as a critical mechanism in several neurodegenerative diseases, and the modulation of signaling pathways associated with inflammation is being explored as a potential strategy for new therapeutics. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the neuroinflammation hypothesis also starts to influence the landscape of drug discovery in place of the previously regarded amyloid hypothesis. As such, the objective of this review is to compile recent advanced in the discovery of anti-neuroinflammatory compounds developed through chemical synthesis and structural modification, providing an overview of current trends in drug discovery strategies and scaffold redesign for the development of the next-generation of anti-neuroinflammatory therapeutics. It was found that the compounds described in the publications could be categorized into four groups: modification of natural compounds, rational drug design, drug screening approaches, and drug repurposing. While the categorization seems to be similar to drug discoveries in other fields, with the modification of natural compounds accounting for most publications, specific observations could still be made. Namely, the growing interest in the multitarget-directed ligand approach reflects the increasing recognition of AD as a multifactorial disease. Despite this, further research is required to identify additional effective activities or the appropriate combinations besides anti-neuroinflammatory activity. Lastly, this review also gives brief overview regarding physicochemical properties of central nervous system-active agents, of which anti-neuroinflammatory compounds are parts of, and suggests the adoption of in silico prediction models as screening tools before the use of in vitro or in vivo models.
authors: Paelaong N, Sripha K, Boondam Y.
screening_reason: The review directly focuses on medicinal chemistry and drug discovery strategies targeting anti-neuroinflammatory mechanisms in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、アルツハイマー病（AD）治療における抗神経炎症化合物の創薬研究の現状と将来の展望をまとめたものである。文献で報告されている化合物は、天然物の構造修飾、合理的創薬デザイン、化合物スクリーニング、ドラッグリパーパシングの4つの領域に分類された。ADの多面的な病態に対応するため、マルチターゲット指向型リガンドへの関心が高まっていることが示された。また、中枢神経系作用薬としての物理化学的プロパティの評価や、スクリーニングツールとしてのin silico予測モデルの活用が提唱されている。
summary_en: This review summarizes recent trends and therapeutic strategies in discovering anti-neuroinflammatory compounds for Alzheimer's disease. The surveyed approaches were categorized into natural product modification, rational drug design, high-throughput screening, and drug repurposing. The authors highlight the potential of multitarget-directed ligands and advocate for integrating in silico prediction tools early in the drug discovery process.
key_finding_ja: アルツハイマー病に対する抗神経炎症化合物の創薬アプローチを4分類に整理し、マルチターゲット指向型設計やin silico予測モデルの導入が重要であることを提示した。
why_it_matters_ja: アルツハイマー病に対する神経炎症を標的とした新薬開発の方向性やスクリーニング手法の最適化に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Associations of self-reported and actigraphic sleep with gut microbiome composition and diversity among older adults.
abstract: Study objectives Poor sleep is linked to adverse health outcomes. Animal studies suggest the gut microbiome may influence sleep, but human findings remain inconsistent. We examined associations of self-reported insomnia symptoms, daytime sleepiness, and actigraphy-measured sleep with gut microbiome diversity and composition in older adults. Methods We studied 869 Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging participants with self-reported sleep and shotgun metagenomic sequencing; 332 also had actigraphy. We tested associations of sleep with alpha diversity, beta diversity, and species composition using regression, PERMANOVA, and ANCOM-BC2, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, physical activity, education, and depressive symptoms. Results Participants had mean age 70.7 years; 54.8% were female and 66.9% White. Trouble falling asleep ≥5 times/week was associated with higher Shannon diversity (β=0.41 SD; 95% CI: 0.09, 0.73) and Pielou's evenness, but not richness metrics. No actigraphy-measured sleep variables were associated with alpha or beta diversity. Beta diversity analyses suggested excessive sleepiness (1-2 o 3-4 times/week) was associated with different microbial composition, though variance explained was small. In species-level analyses, frequent insomnia symptoms or excessive sleepiness were associated with depleted or undetected Eubacterium sp. CAG:251. In exploratory actigraphy models, each doubling of sleep efficiency was associated with higher Eubacterium sp. CAG:251 prevalence (PR=2.15; 95% CI: 1.47, 3.14), while each 30-minute increase in wake after sleep onset was associated with lower prevalence (PR=0.49; 95% CI: 0.29, 0.81). Conclusions Global diversity findings were limited and inconsistent, whereas subjective and objective sleep disturbances converged on Eubacterium sp. CAG:251. Findings are exploratory and require longitudinal replication.
authors: Tilves C, Holingue C, Wanigatunga SK, Chia CW, Zhao N, Wu MN, Schrack JA, Simonsick EM, Ferrucci L, Tanaka T, Spira AP, Mueller NT.
screening_reason: The paper directly investigates the association between sleep parameters and gut microbiome diversity and species composition in older adults.
summary_ja: 高齢者869名を対象に、主観的評価およびアクチグラフィによる睡眠データと腸内細菌叢の関連を横断的に解析しました。全体の菌叢多様性との関連は限定的で一貫性を欠く一方、不眠症状や過度な昼間の眠気の双方が特定腸内細菌Eubacterium sp. CAG:251の検出低下と関連していました。さらに探索的な解析では、アクチグラフィで測定した睡眠効率の高さが本菌種の存在確率の上昇と関連していました。
summary_en: This study examined associations between self-reported or actigraphy-measured sleep parameters and gut microbiome characteristics in 869 older adults. While overall diversity findings were limited, both subjective and objective measures of sleep disturbance consistently converged on lower relative abundance or prevalence of Eubacterium sp. CAG:251. Higher sleep efficiency was linked to increased prevalence of this specific bacterial species.
key_finding_ja: 高齢者において、主観的および客観的な睡眠障害指標が特定腸内細菌Eubacterium sp. CAG:251の減少と一貫して関連していた。
why_it_matters_ja: 睡眠障害と特定の腸内細菌種との関連を示した本結果は、今後の縦断的研究を通じた腸脳相関の解明に寄与することが期待されます。

title: Molecular Editing Reveals a Bilobalide Chemotype that Attenuates Prolyl Endopeptidase (PREP)-Linked Neuroinflammation.
abstract: Natural products offer privileged three-dimensional chemotypes for drug discovery, yet scaffold lability and limited analogue space often impede mechanism-guided optimization. Herein, we show that molecular editing can reveal a natural product-derived chemotype that attenuates neuroinflammation via prolyl endopeptidase (PREP) inhibition. BB10, a chemically stabilized bilobalide analogue generated via lactone-to-lactam molecular editing, significantly suppressed LPS-induced microglial activation and reduced levels of key inflammatory mediators. Unbiased cellular target identification (CETSA-MS) identified PREP as the top thermally stabilized target, supporting cellular target engagement. BB10 inhibited PREP activity in both cellular and recombinant enzyme assays, implicating PREP inhibition as a mechanism contributing to its anti-neuroinflammatory activity. Guided by this target-based insight, structural optimization afforded a fluorinated analogue, BB56, with improved PREP inhibition and superior anti-inflammatory efficacy. Mechanistically, BB56 attenuated p38/NF-κB signaling and reduced NLRP3 upregulation, and PREP knockdown abrogated the anti-inflammatory effects. Finally, BB56 provided functional rescue in a zebrafish model of neuroinflammation. Collectively, this work establishes a molecular editing-enabled approach to a natural product chemotype that modulates neuroinflammation through PREP inhibition.
authors: Sillapachaiyaporn C, Wang W, Qin Y, Yan L, Scheeff S, He X, Wu Q, Lin Y, Shang J, Ye X, Liu J, Sun K, Yeung CW, Huang J, Chen Z, Liu X, Geng Y, Au SWN, Ip BY, Ko H, Ng BW.
screening_reason: The study investigates a stabilized natural product analogue targeting prolyl endopeptidase to suppress microglial activation and neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: 天然物ビロバライドの分子編集により、プロリルエンドペプチダーゼ（PREP）を阻害する化学修飾体BB10が創出された。標的網羅的解析からPREPが直接の標的として同定され、PREP阻害が抗神経炎症作用に寄与することが示された。さらに最適化されたフッ素化誘導体BB56は、p38/NF-κBシグナル伝達とNLRP3の上昇を抑制し、ゼブラフィッシュの神経炎症モデルにおいて機能的回復をもたらした。PREPのノックダウンにより抗炎症効果が消失したことから、PREPを介した神経炎症制御メカニズムが実証された。
summary_en: Molecular editing of bilobalide generated BB10, a lactam analogue that suppresses LPS-induced microglial activation by targeting prolyl endopeptidase (PREP). Structural optimization produced BB56, which demonstrated enhanced PREP inhibition, attenuated p38/NF-κB signaling, and reduced NLRP3 upregulation. Furthermore, BB56 provided functional rescue in a zebrafish neuroinflammation model, highlighting PREP inhibition as a therapeutic target for neuroinflammatory pathways.
key_finding_ja: ビロバライド誘導体BB56はプロリルエンドペプチダーゼ（PREP）を阻害し、p38/NF-κBおよびNLRP3経路を抑えてゼブラフィッシュの神経炎症を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 本研究はPREP阻害を通じた神経炎症制御の可能性を示しており、ミクログリアの過剰活性化に伴う神経炎症性疾患の創薬研究に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Luteolin and neurodegenerative disease modulation: linking molecular mechanisms, neurotransmission, and pharmacokinetics.
abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders arise from the convergence of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, synaptic dysfunction, mitochondrial failure, and dysregulated cell death, highlighting the need for therapeutic agents capable of coordinated, multi-target modulation. Luteolin (3',4',5,7-tetrahydroxyflavone), a dietary flavonoid widely present in edible and medicinal plants, has emerged as a promising neuroactive compound with pleiotropic biological actions. Rather than focusing on isolated outcomes, this review presents an integrated summary of how luteolin orchestrates interconnected signaling networks, with receptor-level neuromodulation and neuroimmune regulation to preserve neuronal integrity. Particular emphasis is placed on pathway convergence, cross-talk, and system-level neuroprotection across models of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related disorders. In parallel, pharmacokinetic behavior, metabolite activity, and emerging delivery strategies are examined in relation to mechanistic efficacy. By linking molecular signaling, neurotransmission and therapeutic feasibility within a unified framework, this review offers a refined perspective on role of luteolin in neurodegenerative disease modulation.
authors: Chib S, Shukla S, Sharma K, Singh R.
screening_reason: The review centrally covers molecular mechanisms of neuroinflammation and neuroimmune regulation in neurodegenerative diseases.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、アルツハイマー病やパーキンソン病などの神経変性疾患モデルにおけるルテオリンの多角的な神経保護作用をまとめたものです。ルテオリンは、受容体レベルでの神経調節や神経免疫系の調整を通じて、相互に関連する複数のシグナル伝達ネットワークを統合的に制御します。さらに、薬物動態学的特性、代謝物の活性、新たなドラッグデリバリー技術と臨床的有効性との関連についても議論されています。
summary_en: This review summarizes the multi-target neuroprotective role of luteolin across models of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Luteolin coordinates interconnected signaling networks, receptor-level neuromodulation, and neuroimmune regulation to preserve neuronal integrity. Pharmacokinetic features, active metabolites, and emerging delivery strategies are also evaluated within a unified therapeutic framework.
key_finding_ja: 天然フラボノイドであるルテオリンは、受容体調律および神経免疫調節を包括的に制御することで神経変性に対する保護効果を発揮することが提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: ルテオリンの作用機序と薬物動態の統合的評価は、複合的病態を示す神経変性疾患に対する多標的天然化合物の応用研究を促進する可能性があります。

title: Integrative transcriptomic and genetic analysis implicates fatty acid metabolic reprogramming in perivascular macrophages in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Dysregulated lipid metabolism and neuroinflammation are increasingly recognized as interacting contributors to Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the cell-type-specific genetic links between fatty acid metabolism and AD remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify fatty acid metabolism-related genes associated with AD risk and to characterize their relevance to perivascular macrophage (PVM) states. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE160936 and bulk transcriptomic data from GSE270454 were integrated to evaluate cell-type-specific fatty acid metabolism activity in AD and control samples.The primary data sources, fatty acid metabolism gene set, AUCell scoring strategy, CellChat workflow, GSEA resources, and MR software settings were specified to improve reproducibility. PVMs were further analyzed for differential expression, ligand-receptor communication, pathway enrichment, transcription factor regulation, and pseudotime-associated transcriptional changes. Cis-eQTL-based two-sample Mendelian randomization was performed using eQTLGen exposure data and AD GWAS summary statistics, followed by sensitivity analyses, reverse MR, and Bayesian colocalization.The analyses were interpreted across three distinct evidence levels: cell-type-resolved transcriptional association, systemic genetic expression prioritization, and tissue-level protein expression. Nominal MR findings were interpreted alongside multiple-testing considerations and colocalization support.Candidate protein expression was examined in hippocampal tissue from APP/PS1 and wild-type mice by Western blotting. Single-cell analysis identified eight major cell populations and showed increased fatty acid metabolism activity in PVMs from AD samples. Mendelian randomization prioritized ten fatty acid metabolism-related genes associated with AD risk, among which ACSL1, EPM2AIP1, MALT1, and RASGRP3 showed strong colocalization support (PP.H4 > 0.9). Pathway analyses linked these genes to lipid metabolic regulation, inflammatory signaling, phagocytosis, and mitochondrial/peroxisomal fatty acid metabolism. Co-expression analysis suggested associations between MALT1 and fatty acid oxidation-related genes, including ACADM and ACOX1. Western blotting in whole hippocampal lysates from APP/PS1 mice provided exploratory tissue-level protein evidence, showing increased ACSL1 and MALT1 and decreased RASGRP3 expression; these findings should not be interpreted as confirmatory PVM-specific validation. This integrative analysis prioritizes ACSL1, EPM2AIP1, MALT1, and RASGRP3 as candidate genes connecting fatty acid metabolic dysregulation with AD-associated neuroinflammatory processes. Because the genetic instruments were blood-derived and the protein assays used whole hippocampal lysates, the findings should be interpreted as candidate-gene prioritization and hypothesis generation rather than proof of direct PVM-specific causality.Accordingly, the study supports a prioritized candidate framework for future functional testing, not validated therapeutic targets or direct causal proof.
authors: Wang F, Wang X, Chen Y, Li Q, Wang S, Cai M, Zhao J.
screening_reason: The study investigates perivascular macrophage metabolic alterations and their links to neuroinflammatory processes in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: 本研究は、アルツハイマー病（AD）における脂肪酸代謝障害と血管周囲マクロファージ（PVM）の転写状態との関連を単一細胞およびバルクトランスクリプトーム解析により調査しました。メンデル無作為化および共局在解析を用いて、ADリスクに関連する脂肪酸代謝関連遺伝子としてACSL1、EPM2AIP1、MALT1、RASGRP3が同定されました。また、APP/PS1マウスモデルの海馬組織においてタンパク質発現の変化が探索的に確認されました。これらの結果は、PVMにおける脂肪酸代謝リプログラミングがADの神経炎症過程に関与している可能性を示しています。
summary_en: Integrative transcriptomic and Mendelian randomization analyses were used to identify fatty acid metabolism-related genes linked to Alzheimer's disease risk and perivascular macrophage states. Four candidate genes—ACSL1, EPM2AIP1, MALT1, and RASGRP3—were prioritized with strong genetic colocalization support. The study connects fatty acid metabolic reprogramming in perivascular macrophages with AD-associated neuroinflammatory processes, offering a framework for future functional validation.
key_finding_ja: アルツハイマー病において、血管周囲マクロファージにおける脂肪酸代謝リプログラミングに関連する候補遺伝子群が特定され、神経炎症との関わりが示唆された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脂質代謝と神経炎症をつなぐ分子候補の特定は、アルツハイマー病における新たな病態メカニズムの解明や治療標的探索の基盤となります。

title: Hormonal therapies for endometriosis-associated pain: inflammatory limitations and pharmacological challenges.
abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory and estrogen-dependent disease in which pain remains the leading cause of impaired quality of life. Hormonal therapies constitute the cornerstone of medical management and include progestins, combined estrogen-progestin contraceptives, gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists and antagonists, selective estrogen and progesterone receptor modulators, and aromatase inhibitors. Although these treatments effectively suppress ovarian function and reduce estrogen-dependent lesion activity, their clinical benefits are frequently limited by adverse effects, contraceptive implications, and symptom recurrence after treatment discontinuation. Increasing evidence indicates that the persistence of endometriosis-associated pain cannot be explained solely by hormonal dysregulation. A sustained inflammatory microenvironment, characterized by innate immune cell activation, pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and neuroimmune interactions, contributes to peripheral and central sensitization, thereby limiting the effectiveness of therapies targeting endocrine pathways alone. These disease-driven mechanisms provide a biological explanation for the heterogeneous response to hormonal treatment observed in clinical practice. This review summarizes the mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety profile and limitations of current hormonal therapies for endometriosis-associated pain. In addition, it discusses the inflammatory and neuroimmune mechanisms underlying persistent pain and highlights the rationale for combining endocrine therapies with emerging anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory strategies. Such integrated approaches may improve long-term pain control, reduce recurrence, and contribute to more personalized management of endometriosis.
authors: García-Izquierdo L, Acedo-Santamaría S, García-Belchí C, Martínez-Esparza M.
screening_reason: Focuses on the sustained inflammatory microenvironment and neuroimmune interactions underlying endometriosis-associated pain.
summary_ja: 子宮内膜症に伴う痛みの治療にはホルモン療法が広く用いられますが、副作用や投与中止後の症状再発などの臨床的限界が存在します。痛みの持続にはホルモン調節異常だけでなく、自然免疫の活性化や神経免疫相互作用による末梢および中枢の感作が深く関与しています。本レビューでは、現行のホルモン療法の限界を整理し、持続的な痛みを引き起こす神経免疫・炎症メカニズムについて考察しています。さらに、内分泌療法と免疫調節抗炎症戦略を組み合わせた併用治療アプローチの合理性を提唱しています。
summary_en: Current hormonal therapies for endometriosis-associated pain face limitations due to side effects, contraceptive issues, and post-treatment symptom recurrence. Persistent pain is sustained by a chronic inflammatory microenvironment, innate immune cell activation, and neuroimmune interactions that cause peripheral and central sensitization. Combining endocrine treatments with anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory agents is highlighted as a promising framework to improve long-term pain management.
key_finding_ja: 子宮内膜症に関連する持続的な痛みには神経免疫相互作用や免疫細胞活性化が強く関わっており、内分泌療法と免疫調節療法の併用アプローチが提案されている。
why_it_matters_ja: 神経免疫炎症経路を標的とした併用療法の確立は、従来のホルモン療法で十分な効果が得られない患者に対する個別化治療の進展に役立つ可能性があります。

title: A low-crosslinking hydrogel integrating prodrug nanoparticles modulates neuroinflammation and ECM deposition for enhanced spinal cord regeneration.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes pathological extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition and tissue stiffening, impeding axonal regeneration and disrupting homeostasis. Galardin-mediated inhibition of matrix metalloproteinases reduces ECM deposition and promotes recovery, but systemic administration fails to adequately address local microenvironment deterioration. We therefore explore a localized biomaterial delivery strategy via regulating the crosslinking degree of hydrogel matrix, in which high-crosslinking density of hydrogel (HCGH) tends to exacerbate neuroinflammation via Piezo1 activation as well as Wwtr1-dependent macrophage reprogramming. Based on this, we fabricate an integrated therapeutic platform where pH-responsive curcumin-succinate self-assembled prodrug nanoparticles (co-loaded with Galardin and basic fibroblast growth factor, denoted as CrS-GF NPs) are encapsulated in a low-crosslinking hydrogel (LCGH). By thorough testing on the compression spinal cord injury model of mice, the LCGH@CrS-GF system not only modulates excessive ECM deposition and neuroinflammation, but also provides sufficient neurotrophic support, thereby facilitating smooth axonal regeneration and functional restoration of the damaged spinal cords in a collaborative manner. Our study highlights the importance of using hydrogels with tailored crosslinking density to deliver therapeutics for SCI repair by stimulating beneficial biological responses and manipulating ECM deposition.
authors: Chen X, Wang B, Hui J, Shen W, Xu L, Lai A, Huang R, Yan F, Yao Q, Zhang Z, Xu J, Cai X, Wu F, Hu S, Xiao J, Li Z.
screening_reason: Focuses on localized hydrogel delivery to attenuate neuroinflammation and macrophage response after spinal cord injury.
summary_ja: 脊髄損傷後には細胞外マトリックスの過剰な蓄積や組織の硬化が生じ、軸索再生が阻害されます。研究チームは、高架橋度ヒドロジェルがPiezo1活性化およびマクロファージ再プログラミングを介して神経炎症を悪化させることを見出しました。そこで、ガラージンと塩基性線維芽細胞増殖因子を含むナノ粒子を組み込んだ低架橋度ヒドロジェルを開発しました。マウスの圧迫脊髄損傷モデルにおいて、本システムは神経炎症と過剰なマトリックス蓄積を抑え、神経再生および機能回復を促進しました。
summary_en: High-crosslinking hydrogels were found to exacerbate neuroinflammation after spinal cord injury via Piezo1 activation and macrophage reprogramming. To overcome this, a low-crosslinking hydrogel encapsulating prodrug nanoparticles loaded with Galardin and basic fibroblast growth factor was developed. In a mouse spinal cord compression model, this therapeutic platform modulated neuroinflammation and extracellular matrix deposition while enhancing axonal regeneration and functional recovery.
key_finding_ja: 低架橋度ヒドロジェルとプロドラッグナノ粒子を融合させた送達システムは、マウス脊髄損傷モデルにおいて神経炎症と細胞外マトリックス沈着を抑制し軸索再生を促すことが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 架橋度を最適化したヒドロジェルによる微小環境の調節策は、脊髄損傷に対する新たな局所組織再生治療法の開発に寄与する可能性があります。

title: Air Pollution and Parkinson's Disease Pathology: Clinical Evidence and the Molecular Mechanisms Linking Airborne Toxicants to Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative condition, and its rising prevalence necessitates the urgent need to identify modifiable risk factors. Air pollution, a pervasive and also escalating public health problem, has emerged as a potential contributor to the incidence and progression of PD. As urbanization and industrialization continue to exacerbate global air pollution levels, understanding the relationship between airborne toxicants and PD is a pressing scientific and public health priority. In this review, we critically discuss the current epidemiological evidence and the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying air pollution-induced neurodegeneration in PD. Clinical studies associate long-term interaction with pollutants such as nitrogen oxides, particulate matter, and ozone with increased PD risk. Evidence also suggests that air pollution worsens PD prognosis. Mechanistically, air pollution is hypothesized to contribute to PD pathogenesis through gut microbiome alternations, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammatory pathways, as well as promoting α-synuclein aggregation.
authors: Pakkhesal S, Pourebrahimian Leilabadi S, Hamzehzadeh S, Zare F, Gholipour-Khalili E, Malekinejad F, Fakhkhari S, Talebi M, Naseri A.
screening_reason: Reviews airborne toxicant mechanisms directly driving neuroinflammation and gut microbiome alterations in Parkinson's disease.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、大気汚汚染物質への暴露とパーキンソン病の病態に関する疫学データおよび分子メカニズムをまとめています。窒素酸化物や粒子状物質、オゾンへの長期暴露は、パーキンソン病の発症リスク上昇および症状悪化に関連しています。大気汚染物質は、腸内細菌叢の変化、酸化ストレス、神経炎症経路の活性化、ならびにα-シヌクレイン凝集を促進することで神経変性に関与すると考えられています。
summary_en: This review evaluates the epidemiological and mechanistic evidence connecting long-term air pollution exposure to increased Parkinson's disease risk and severity. Airborne pollutants such as particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, and ozone are hypothesized to drive neurodegeneration through gut microbiome alterations, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and enhanced α-synuclein aggregation.
key_finding_ja: 大気汚染物質への長期的暴露は、腸内細菌叢の変動や神経炎症、α-シヌクレイン凝集などの複合的メカニズムを通じてパーキンソン病リスクを高めることが示唆された。
why_it_matters_ja: 大気汚染が神経変性疾患に与える影響の解明は、環境規制の推進や予防的介入アプローチの立案において重要です。

title: Update on the Pathophysiology of Yellow Fever Intoxication.
abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) remains a major global health threat, driven by climate change, vector expansion, and vaccine shortages. Despite centuries of observation, the pathophysiology of severe yellow fever (YF), specifically the highly lethal "intoxication phase," remains poorly understood. Recent clinical data from the 2016-2019 São Paulo epidemic and advances in animal models have shifted the understanding of YFV from a purely hepatocentric disease to a complex multiorgan syndrome. Emerging evidence indicates that YFV-induced endothelial damage and hypotension trigger profound intestinal ischemia and mucosal barrier breakdown, which allows gut bacteria to translocate into the portal system. Because the YFV-damaged liver cannot clear these pathogens, secondary polymicrobial sepsis ensues, likely contributing to the high mortality rates observed in severe YF. Our proposed gut-centered framework explains the distinct clinical presentation of YF intoxication. Recognizing secondary sepsis and vascular leakage highlights the urgent need for optimized fluid management, early dialysis, and targeted antimicrobial therapies to improve clinical outcomes.
authors: Duarte-Neto AN, Ho YL, Kallas EG, Bailey AL.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Proposes a gut-centered framework where intestinal mucosal barrier breakdown and gut bacterial translocation cause secondary sepsis in yellow fever.
summary_ja: 重症黄熱病（中毒期）の病態生理について、近年の臨床データや動物モデルに基づき考察した解説論文である。黄熱ウイルスによる血管内皮障害と低血圧が著しい腸管虚血と粘膜バリア破綻を引き起こし、腸内細菌が門脈系へ移行することを示している。障害を受けた肝臓がこれら病原体を排除できないため、二段階的に多菌性敗血症が惹起されると提唱している。
summary_en: This review outlines an updated framework for the pathophysiology of severe yellow fever intoxication, shifting the view from a purely hepatocentric disease to a complex multiorgan syndrome. Yellow fever virus-induced endothelial damage and hypotension trigger intestinal ischemia and mucosal barrier collapse, allowing gut bacteria to translocate into the portal system. The impaired liver fails to clear these pathogens, resulting in secondary polymicrobial sepsis.
key_finding_ja: 黄熱ウイルスの重症中毒期において、腸管虚血と粘膜バリア破綻に伴う腸内細菌の移行が二段階的な多菌性敗血症を引き起こすことが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸管主導の病態メカニズムの解明は、重症黄熱病における体液管理や早期透析、標的抗菌療法の最適化に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Targeting chemobrain: from experimental models to therapeutic discovery.
abstract: Chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment affects a substantial proportion of cancer survivors and significantly diminishes quality of life, yet no FDA-approved therapies exist. Chemotherapeutic agents such as cisplatin, doxorubicin, paclitaxel and methotrexate induce oxidative stress, DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation, which disrupt synaptic plasticity and neurogenesis. Key pathways include PARP1 activation, NAD depletion, COX-2 signaling and adenosine A2A receptor dysregulation. Evidence from rodent and complementary models including Drosophila, zebrafish and Caenorhabditis elegans demonstrates conserved mechanisms. We highlight a multi-model discovery pipeline and discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting redox balance, mitochondrial function and neuroinflammatory pathways to mitigate cognitive decline in cancer survivors.
authors: Parikh NN, Kim HG, Sojung Moon AM, Lee SH, Kim SH, Lee E, Rashid MA, Park Y, Steven Zheng XF, Jang MH.
screening_reason: Examines neuroinflammatory pathways and mechanisms underlying chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment.
summary_ja: 本論文は、がんサバイバーの生活の質を著しく低下させる抗がん剤起因性認知機能障害（ケモブレイン）のメカニズムと創薬パイプラインを概説したレビューである。シスプラチン、ドキソルビシン、パクリタキセル、メトトレキサートなどの抗がん剤は、酸化ストレス、DNA損傷、ミトコンドリア障害、神経炎症を引き起こし、シナプス可塑性や神経新生を障害する。PARP1活性化、NAD枯渇、COX-2シグナル、アデノシンA2A受容体異常などが主要な分子経路として挙げられており、齧歯類やショウジョウバエ、ゼブラフィッシュなどのモデル生物研究で保存性が確認されている。酸化還元バランス、ミトコンドリア機能、神経炎症経路を標的とした新たな治療戦略の進展が議論されている。
summary_en: This review discusses the mechanistic drivers of chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment (chemobrain), including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. It highlights conserved pathological pathways across rodent and non-rodent model organisms, such as PARP1 activation and COX-2 signaling. The article outlines therapeutic strategies targeting redox balance, mitochondrial health, and neuroinflammatory pathways to mitigate cognitive decline in cancer survivors.
key_finding_ja: 抗がん剤投与に伴う神経炎症やミトコンドリア障害がケモブレインの主要要因であり、これらを標的とする治療法開発のモデル・パイプラインが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: がんサバイバーにおける認知機能低下を軽減する標的治療薬の開発に向けた基盤となる可能性がある。

title: Quantum and nanoscale sensing of microinflammation for earlier detection of chronic inflammatory and neuroimmune disease.
abstract: Chronic inflammatory diseases may begin with spatially restricted and low-abundance inflammatory events that precede overt symptoms. In this perspective, we refer to such early events as micro-inflammation and discuss how mechanistic insights from the IL-6 amplifier and neuroimmune regulation may guide earlier detection of related diseases. The IL-6 amplifier is a positive-feedback inflammatory circuit in non-immune cells driven by concurrent NF-κB and IL-6-STAT3 signaling, whereas the gateway reflex illustrates how defined neural inputs can induce site-specific vascular micro-inflammation and immune-cell entry into affected tissues and organs. We also discuss stress-associated neuroimmune remodeling in diffuse neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus (dNPSLE) as a representative example of region-specific brain inflammation that may precede overt neuropsychiatric manifestations. On this basis, we examine how quantum and nanoscale sensing platforms, particularly fluorescent nanodiamonds containing nitrogen-vacancy centers and AI-assisted nanopore devices, could be adapted to detect candidate readouts of micro-inflammation, including reactive oxygen species, cytokine-related signals, nucleic acids, and other trace biomarkers. The original contribution of this Perspective is a mechanistically guided framework that maps micro-inflammatory biology related to the IL-6 amplifier, the gateway reflex, and dNPSLE onto specific classes of candidate nanosensing readouts, including oxidative stress-related physicochemical signals, cytokine-associated soluble biomarkers, extracellular nucleic acids, and other trace molecular signatures. Rather than providing a comprehensive review of all inflammatory mechanisms or diagnostic technologies, we present a mechanistically focused perspective linking neuroimmunology to next-generation sensing. We also highlight current limitations, including the predominantly preclinical nature of supporting evidence, uncertainty regarding accessible blood or cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers at presymptomatic stages, and the challenge of translating spatially restricted inflammatory signals into non-invasive human diagnostics.
authors: Tanaka Y, Wang Y, Tanaka H, Hojyo S, Kamiya N, Murakami K, Murakami M.
screening_reason: Develops a biosensing framework based directly on neuroimmune regulation, the gateway reflex, and neuroimmunological biology.
summary_ja: 本パースペクティブ論文は、慢性炎症性疾患や神経免疫疾患の発症前に生じる局所的かつ微量な「微小炎症」を早期検出するための量子・ナノセンシング技術の概念枠組みを提示している。IL-6アンプリファイアーやゲートウェイ反射、神経精神全身性エリテマトーデス（dNPSLE）における神経免疫リモデリングの生物学的メカニズムに基づき、それらをセンシング技術と結びつけている。窒素-空孔中心を持つ蛍光ナノダイヤモンドやAI支援ナノポアデバイスなどの技術が、活性酸素種やサイトカイン、細胞外核酸などの極微量バイオマーカー検出に応用可能であると論じている。一方で、前臨床データの依存性や生体試料におけるプレ臨床段階でのバイオマーカーアクセシビリティなど、実用化に向けた課題も指摘されている。
summary_en: This perspective presents a mechanistically guided framework linking neuroimmune micro-inflammation to quantum and nanoscale sensing platforms for early disease detection. The authors discuss how molecular mechanisms like the IL-6 amplifier and gateway reflex map onto readout signals suitable for technologies such as fluorescent nanodiamonds and nanopore devices. Current limitations include reliance on preclinical data and challenges in translating localized signals into non-invasive human diagnostics.
key_finding_ja: IL-6アンプリファイアーやゲートウェイ反射などの神経免疫機構に基づく微小炎症を、量子およびナノスケールセンシングで捉える早期診断枠組みが提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 症候化前の微少な神経炎症現象を捉えるセンシング技術が確立されれば、慢性炎症疾患や神経免疫疾患の超早期介入に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Probiotic Bacillus strains enhance cellulose digestibility and silkworms growth via gut microbiota modulation.
abstract: Dietary supplementation with probiotics has been demonstrated to enhance nutritional efficiency and economic traits in the silkworms (Bombyx mori), with mechanistic insights indicating that these benefits are associated with gut microbiota activity and mucosal immune modulation through the regulation of enzymatic functions. This study investigated the effects of probiotic Bacillus species on intestinal microbiome diversity in fifth-instar silkworms. Two native isolates, Bacillus subtilis Y11 and Bacillus velezensis Z55, were administered either individually or in combination to experimental groups (CK, Y11, Z55, and Y11/Z55) on the first day of the fifth instar. Intestinal contents were collected at days 1, 3, and 5 after treatment for 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and cellulose content in silkworm excrement was measured on a daily basis. Experimental groups exhibited significantly elevated body weight, digestive capacity, and cocoon weight compared to controls. The cellulose content in silkworm excrement decreased by 24.7% and 31.8% on days 2 and 3, respectively, compared to the control (CK) group at the corresponding time points. Tax4Fun2 analysis further predicted a rapid increase in the potential abundance of cellulose degradation-related genes within the gut microbiome, an inference based on taxonomic composition. These findings support the hypothesis that probiotic treatment may enhance the net efficiency of cellulose degradation in silkworms by modulating the gut microbial community and structure, thereby offering new insights into improving their growth performance.
authors: Jin Y, Zhao Y, Chen C, Jiang X, Chen S, Zhang R, Li H, Gui Z.
screening_reason: Focuses on gut microbiota modulation and microbial metabolic gene enhancement by probiotic Bacillus strains.
summary_ja: 本研究は、カイコ（Bombyx mori）の5齢幼虫において、プロバイオティクスであるBacillus subtilis Y11およびBacillus velezensis Z55の投与が腸内細菌叢とセルロース消化に与える影響を検証した。これらのBacillus菌株を単独または組み合わせて投与した結果、対照群と比較して体重、消化能、繭重が有意に増加した。フン中のセルロース含有量は投与後2日目および3日目で著しく減少した。さらにメタゲノム予測解析により、腸内細菌叢におけるセルロース分解関連遺伝子の潜在的豊度の上昇が示された。
summary_en: Dietary administration of probiotic Bacillus strains, individually or in combination, improved body weight, digestive capacity, and cocoon weight in fifth-instar silkworms. Probiotic treatment reduced excrement cellulose content and predicted an increase in cellulose degradation-related genes in the gut microbiome. These results suggest that Bacillus probiotics enhance cellulose degradation efficiency by modulating the intestinal microbial community.
key_finding_ja: プロバイオティクスであるBacillus菌株の投与により、カイコの腸内細菌叢の構造が変化し、セルロースの分解効率と成長パフォーマンスが向上した。
why_it_matters_ja: 昆虫の腸内微生物叢制御を通じた養蚕業の生産性向上や飼料効率改善への応用が期待される。

title: Nucleic acid based profile of body surface and gut bacteria among wall gecko: a potential hub for antibiotic resistance dissemination within household.
abstract: Background Wall gecko (WG) (Hemidactylus frenatus), a common reptile seen around human dwellings within tropics, subtropics, as well as warm/coastal regions and countries is a genre of reptile, often seen as harmless, yet reported as potential reservoir of resistant bacteria housed on body-surface and gastrointestinal-tract (GIT). Methods This pilot study evaluates the antibiotic-resistance-index (ARI) and gene profiles of bacterial species isolated from body-surface and GIT of WG captured from residential environments at Abraka, Ethiope East Local government area, Delta state, Nigeria. Five representative WG were captured from study area between 16th may and 30th august 2025. Triplicate collected swab samples from skin and GIT-tissue were cultured onto growth media. Using standard Microbiological procedures (Gram-staining, biochemical tests etc.), preliminary bacteria identification were conducted. Kirby-Bauer-disk-diffusion method of Antibiotic-susceptibility-testing was performed and ARI were calculated to assess environmental antibiotic-resistance implication. Molecular biology analysis of antibiotic-resistant (AR) strains using Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) (including DNA extraction, target-gene amplification) sequencing and phylogenetics analyses were performed to confirm isolates/gene identity. Results This investigation revealed strains of Staphylococcus aureus, Acinetobacter nosocomialis, Mammaliicoccus sciuri, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli. High ARI were recorded for Escherichia coli (0.8). The molecular analysis revealed presence of AR-genes including mecA, ermA, SHV, CTX-M, OXA, KPC, AMPC, ermC and blaTEM genes among isolates. Conclusion These findings highlight the role of WGs as potential reservoir and disseminator of multidrug-resistant bacteria. The need for public health awareness and integrated pest-pathogen control strategies is highly recommended especially among household/environments were wall-gecko is prevalent.
authors: Owhe-Ureghe UB, Igere BE, Orutugu LA, Brisibe EO, Ukwamedua CM, Ogbe VO, Jonathan EO, Ichipi RP.
screening_reason: Investigates gut bacteria and gastrointestinal tract microbial resistance profiles in wall geckos.
summary_ja: 住宅周囲に棲息するホオグロヤモリの体表および消化管から分離された細菌の抗生物質耐性指標（ARI）と耐性遺伝子プロファイルを調べたパイロット研究です。ナイジェリアで捕獲されたヤモリから、大腸菌、黄色ブドウ球菌、Klebsiella pneumoniaeなどが同定され、特に大腸菌において高いARI（0.8）が記録されました。分子生物学解析により、mecA、ermA、CTX-M、blaTEMなどの多岐にわたる薬剤耐性遺伝子の存在が確認されました。
summary_en: This pilot study assessed the antibiotic resistance index (ARI) and resistance gene profiles of bacteria isolated from the body surface and gastrointestinal tract of wall geckos captured around human dwellings. Identified bacterial species included Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Klebsiella pneumoniae, with E. coli showing a high ARI of 0.8. Molecular analyses detected multiple resistance genes, including mecA, ermA, CTX-M, and blaTEM, among the isolates.
key_finding_ja: 住宅付近のヤモリの体表および消化管細菌から複数の薬剤耐性遺伝子が高頻度で検出され、多剤耐性菌のリザーバーとなっている可能性が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 家庭環境における耐性菌蔓延のリスク評価および公衆衛生管理や害虫・病原体対策の設計に寄与する可能性があります。

title: Celiac Disease and the Nervous System: A Comprehensive Overview of Neurological Manifestations and Underlying Mechanisms.
abstract: Celiac disease (CD) is a chronic immune-mediated enteropathy triggered by gluten ingestion in genetically susceptible individuals. While traditionally associated with gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms, CD is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder with significant neurological involvement. A growing body of evidence links CD to a broad spectrum of neurological manifestations, including gluten ataxia (GA), peripheral neuropathy (PN), epilepsy, migraine, myoclonic disorders, and cognitive impairment. These symptoms may precede or occur independently of GI symptoms, complicating diagnosis and delaying treatment. The underlying mechanisms are multifactorial, involving autoantibody cross-reactivity, neuroinflammation, increased permeability of the intestinal and blood-brain barrier (BBB), gut dysbiosis, and micronutrient deficiencies. This review synthesizes current insights into the pathophysiological basis of CD-related neurological disorders. We also explore the therapeutic impact of a strict gluten-free diet (GFD) on CD-related neurological manifestations. Early recognition of neurological signs and their prompt management are essential to mitigate irreversible neural injury and improve long-term outcomes in these patients. Given the potential for symptom reversibility with dietary treatment, routine screening for CD should be considered in patients presenting with idiopathic neurological syndromes, even in the absence of GI symptoms.
authors: Yousefzadeh Eshkoori A, Mahmoudi Ghehsareh M, Asri N, Jahani-Sherafat S, Rezaei Tavirani M, Zali A, Amiri M, Monazami A, Rostami-Nejad M.
screening_reason: The review explicitly addresses neuroinflammation, gut dysbiosis, and intestinal permeability in the pathogenesis of celiac-related neurological manifestations.
summary_ja: セリアック病（CD）は消化器症状だけでなく、グルテン失調症や末梢神経障害など多様な神経症状を伴う全身性疾患である。その病態メカニズムには、自己抗体の交差反応、神経炎症、腸管および血液脳関門の透過性亢進、腸内細菌叢異常、微量栄養素欠乏などが複雑に関与する。厳格なグルテンフリー食事療法が神経症状の改善に与える影響が提示されている。消化器症状がない原因不明の神経症候群患者においてもセリアック病の早期スクリーニングが推奨される。
summary_en: This review synthesizes the neurological manifestations associated with celiac disease, including gluten ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, and cognitive impairment. The complex mechanisms involve autoantibody cross-reactivity, neuroinflammation, barrier permeability alterations, dysbiosis, and nutritional deficits. The authors emphasize that early recognition and a strict gluten-free diet are crucial for preventing irreversible neural damage.
key_finding_ja: セリアック病に伴う神経障害は自己抗体交差反応や神経炎症などの多因子的メカニズムで生じ、早期のグルテンフリー食事療法により回復する可能性がある。
why_it_matters_ja: 消化器症状を伴わない特発性神経疾患患者においてもセリアック病を疑うことで、早期介入による不可逆的な神経障害の抑制につながる可能性がある。

title: Pathogenic mechanisms of Aeromonas hydrophila and the protective role of probiotics in sustainable aquaculture.
abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila (A. hydrophila) is a pervasive opportunistic fish pathogen responsible for hemorrhagic septicemia and gastrointestinal disease and, together with other motile aeromonads (e.g., A. veronii, A. caviae, and A. dhakensis), for motile aeromonad septicemia (MAS), which cause significant economic losses in the global freshwater aquaculture industry. The widespread use of antibiotics to control A. hydrophila has led to increased antimicrobial resistance and environmental concerns, necessitating the urgent need for sustainable alternative treatments. We systematically retrieved, screened, and selected relevant studies from three databases: Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed. Articles published between January 1, 2016, and June 1, 2026, were included. Two reviewers independently assessed the eligibility and data quality and extracted information from the identified articles. We performed a bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and RStudio for visualization. We identified 339 experimental research publications from 2016 to 2026 and selected 39 articles that met the selection criteria for full-text evaluation. For VOSviewer keyword co-occurrence networking, we used the 277 Scopus publications (research articles, reviews, and book chapters) retrieved with the same search string. For the country trend analysis, we used the 464 deduplicated records (research articles, reviews, and book chapters) screened after duplicate removal. The most current keywords used were A. hydrophila, probiotic agents, microbiology, and probiotics. The country trend analysis revealed a remarkable increase in publications over the past 10 years, with key contributions from China, India, Iran, Brazil, and Egypt. The year 2025 recorded the highest publication output over the past 10 years. A diverse repertoire of virulence factors, including act, aerA, fla, ahyI, ahyR, and type III secretion systems, mediates A. hydrophila pathogenicity. Probiotics exert consistent multimodal protection via competitive pathogen exclusion, production of antimicrobial compounds, intestinal barrier enhancement, and host immunomodulation. Probiotics improve growth performance, digestive enzyme production, nutritional composition, immune response, hematology and histopathology, gut microbiome, and survival. This review highlights that probiotics are a viable, evidence-based component of integrated health management programs for A. hydrophila control, complementing rather than universally replacing antibiotics. This review highlights that probiotics are viable, evidence-based, and sustainable alternatives to antibiotics for A. hydrophila control.
authors: Ayana GU, Abdullateef MM, Yadata GW, Manzoor R, Sumana SL, Gelata AM, Islam MM.
screening_reason: Focuses on gut microbiome modulation and intestinal mucosal interactions by probiotics against Aeromonas hydrophila.
summary_ja: 本論文は、淡水養殖において深刻な損失を引き起こすエロモナス・ヒドロフィラ（Aeromonas hydrophila）の病原性機構と、プロバイオティクスによる保護作用に関する研究動向を包括的に概括したレビューである。2016年から2026年までの文献データベースから抽出した研究を対象に、ビブリオメトリクス分析とフルテキスト評価を実施した。A. hydrophilaはactやaerA、III型分泌装置などの病原性因子を介して感染を引き起こすが、プロバイオティクスは病原体の競合的排除や抗菌物質産生、腸管バリアの増強、免疫調節などを通じて多角的な防御効果を示すことが整理された。プロバイオティクスは抗生物質を完全に置き換えるものではなく、統合的な健康管理プログラムの補完的かつ有効な代替手段として位置づけられる。
summary_en: This review systematically analyzes the pathogenic mechanisms of Aeromonas hydrophila and the protective role of probiotics in freshwater aquaculture based on literature published between 2016 and 2026. The findings indicate that probiotics provide multimodal protection through competitive pathogen exclusion, intestinal barrier enhancement, and host immunomodulation. Probiotics represent a viable, evidence-based component of integrated health management to complement antibiotic use.
key_finding_ja: プロバイオティクスは競合的排除、抗菌物質の産生、腸管バリアの強化、免疫調節を介してエロモナス・ヒドロフィラに対する多角的な防御効果を発揮する。
why_it_matters_ja: 抗生物質耐性のリスクを低減しつつ、持続可能な淡水養殖の健康管理体系を構築するための基礎的知見となる可能性がある。

title: Hemerocallis lilioasphodelus root water extract ameliorates non-alcoholic fatty liver disease by regulating the gut-liver axis and activating AMPK-mediated lipid metabolism: an integrated study based on metabolomics and 16S rRNA sequencing.
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Hemerocallis lilioasphodelus L. is a traditional medicinal herb used for liver and spleen disorders. However, its pharmacological effects and underlying mechanisms against nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) remain unclear. Aim of the study This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of Hemerocallis lilioasphodelus root water extract (HL) against high-fat diet (HFD) induced NAFLD in mice and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Materials and methods The chemical constituents of HL were analyzed using UHPLC-QE-MS technology, and a NAFLD mouse model was established through HFD induction, followed by HL intervention. By integrating serum pharmacochemistry, network pharmacology, and multi-omics techniques, combined with in vivo and in vitro experimental validation, this study systematically elucidates the mechanism by which HL ameliorates NAFLD. Results A total of 143 active components were identified in HL, 15 of which were absorbed into the bloodstream. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that the AMPK signaling pathway may be associated with the therapeutic effects of HL against NAFLD. In vivo experiments confirmed that HL significantly ameliorated HFD-induced dyslipidemia, hepatic lipid accumulation, and histopathological injury in mice. Mechanistically, HL suppressed de novo lipogenesis by activating the hepatic AMPK/SREBP1c axis. Furthermore, HL treatment remodeled the gut microbiota specifically enriching Akkermansia and strengthened the intestinal barrier, thereby reducing the translocation of gut-derived harmful signals to the liver. Conclusion HL presumably ameliorates NAFLD by regulating the AMPK signaling pathway and intestinal microbiota homeostasis, providing an important basis for further research on the treatment of NAFLD with HL.
authors: Zhang L, Lin S, Li J, Wang Z, Cui H, Bao F, Di Y, Xu C, Dai T, Yuan H, Piao G.
screening_reason: Examines how an herbal extract ameliorates NAFLD via remodeling gut microbiota composition and preserving intestinal barrier integrity.
summary_ja: 高脂血症食（HFD）誘発非アルコール性脂肪性肝疾患（NAFLD）マウスモデルを用いて、ノカンゾウ根水抽出物（HL）の保護効果と作用機序を解析した研究です。HL投与は、肝臓のAMPK/SREBP1c経路の活性化を通じて脂肪の新生を抑制し、脂質異常症および肝脂質蓄積を改善しました。さらに、HLは腸内細菌叢の構成を変化させ、Akkermansia属菌を特異的に増加させるとともに腸管バリア機能を強化しました。これにより、腸由来の有害シグナルが肝臓へ移行するのを抑制することが示されました。
summary_en: This study investigated the protective effects of Hemerocallis lilioasphodelus root water extract (HL) against high-fat diet-induced NAFLD in mice. HL treatment suppressed hepatic de novo lipogenesis via the AMPK/SREBP1c axis and significantly ameliorated dyslipidemia and hepatic lipid accumulation. Additionally, HL restored gut microbiota homeostasis by enriching Akkermansia and strengthened the intestinal barrier, reducing harmful signal translocation to the liver.
key_finding_ja: ノカンゾウ根水抽出物は、肝臓のAMPK経路の活性化とAkkermansia属菌の増殖を伴う腸内細菌叢の再編成を介してNAFLDを改善することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢と腸管バリア機能の調節を介した脂肪性肝疾患の新たな生薬療法の開発に寄与する可能性があります。

title: Gestational diabetes mellitus amplifies sevoflurane-induced developmental neurotoxicity in offspring mice.
abstract: Objective Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) may increase offspring susceptibility to neurodevelopmental stressors. Sevoflurane is widely used in pediatric anesthesia but carries potential neurotoxicity risks. This study investigated whether maternal GDM exacerbates sevoflurane-induced developmental neurotoxicity in offspring, and explored the underlying mechanisms related to neuroinflammation, microglial activation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Methods A mouse model of maternal GDM was established, and offspring received sevoflurane exposure during brain development. Cognitive function was assessed by behavioral tests. Neuronal apoptosis and dendritic spine morphology were detected by TUNEL and Golgi-Cox staining. Microglial activation and inflammatory profiles were analyzed using immunofluorescence and multiplex liquid-chip assays. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were integrated to identify dysregulated molecular pathways, and key proteins were verified by Western Blot. Results Compared with control and single-treatment groups, combined GDM and sevoflurane exposure significantly worsened long-term cognitive impairment, promoted neuronal apoptosis, and reduced dendritic spine density in the hippocampus. The dual-hit induced robust microglial overactivation and disrupted inflammatory cytokine homeostasis. Multi-omics analyses revealed significant enrichment of pathways governing synaptic vesicle cycling, glutamatergic synaptic function, and immune-inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, the dual-hit caused severe mitochondrial dynamic imbalance characterized by downregulation of the fusion protein Mfn2, together with abnormal expression of the microglial receptor CX3CR1. Conclusion Maternal GDM exposure is associated with aggravated sevoflurane-induced developmental neurotoxicity in offspring. Our correlative findings suggest potential underlying links involving altered mitochondrial homeostasis and excessive microglial activation. This study provides potential targets for preventing anesthesia-related neurotoxicity in high-risk children.
authors: Sun X, Fang X, Pan Y, Zheng Y, Lu Y, Guo X, Hu X, Xu Z.
screening_reason: Investigates microglial overactivation, neuroinflammation, and synaptic dysregulation in gestational diabetes and anesthesia-induced developmental neurotoxicity.
summary_ja: 母体における妊娠糖尿病（GDM）と子マウスの発達期セボフルラン曝露の複合的影響を検証した研究です。単独処理と比較して、GDMとセボフルランの複合曝露は子マウスの長期的認知機能障害、海馬における神経細胞アポトーシス、樹状突起スパイン密度の減少を悪化させました。さらに、ミクログリアの過剰活性化や炎症性サイトカインの恒常性破壊、ミトコンドリア融合タンパク質Mfn2の低下、CX3CR1の発現異常が認められました。マルチオミクス解析では、シナプス小胞リサイクルや免疫・炎症反応に関わる経路の濃縮が示されました。
summary_en: This study evaluated the combined impact of maternal gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and developmental sevoflurane exposure in offspring mice. Dual exposure exacerbated long-term cognitive impairment, neuronal apoptosis, and dendritic spine loss in the hippocampus compared to control or single exposures. Microglial overactivation, disrupted cytokine homeostasis, Mfn2 downregulation, and altered CX3CR1 expression were identified as potential underlying mechanisms.
key_finding_ja: 妊娠糖尿病モデルのマウスにおいて、発達期のセボフルラン曝露がミクログリア過剰活性化やミトコンドリア動態不全を伴って海馬障害および認知機能悪化を著しく増幅させることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 妊娠糖尿病が小児麻酔に関連する発達期神経毒性のリスクを高める可能性を示唆しており、高リスク児に対する保護戦略の開発に寄与することが期待されます。

title: Corrigendum to Porphyromonas gingivalis -Induced NETs Mediate Neuroinflammation via TLR4 Activation.
screening_reason: This corrigendum relates to a study examining how neutrophil extracellular traps mediate neuroinflammation via TLR4 activation.
summary_ja: 本報告は、Porphyromonas gingivalisが誘導するNETsがTLR4活性化を介して神経炎症を及ぼす機序に関する研究論文の訂正報告である。出版された原著論文の修正事項が示されている。抄録の本文は含まれていない。
summary_en: This document serves as a corrigendum to a research paper on Porphyromonas gingivalis-induced NETs mediating neuroinflammation via TLR4 activation. No abstract text is included.
key_finding_ja: 歯周病菌誘導NETsとTLR4を介した神経炎症に関する論文の訂正報告である。
why_it_matters_ja: 公表された研究成果の正確性を保証し、学術的整合性を保つために不可欠な訂正である。

title: Targeting Mitochondria for Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction: From Mechanisms to Therapeutics.
abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is a frequent neurological complication in older surgical patients, leading to substantial declines in quality of life and placing a considerable burden on society. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to POCD, including disrupted energy metabolism, excessive reactive oxygen species production, calcium imbalance, and abnormalities in mitochondrial dynamics and quality control processes. These mitochondrial impairments further trigger neuroinflammation and activate multiple cell death pathways. In addition, the review examines current mitochondria-targeted therapeutic strategies and their underlying mechanisms, highlighting the neuroprotective roles of agents such as SS-31, Mdivi-1, P110, and NLRP3 inhibitors in preclinical studies. It also explores the promise of multi-target combinational treatments, time-specific interventions, and individualized therapeutic approaches.
